lineas.texto: How does plain soap beat so many viruses?
Many viruses wear a thin coat of fat around them.
And one end of a soap molecule is a tail that loves fat.
Those tails dig into the fatty coat.
They pry it apart, and the virus falls to pieces.
The pieces get trapped inside tiny balls of soap.
Then the rinse carries them down the drain.
That's why you scrub for twenty seconds. The soap needs time to work.
